subject: Private deployment: bandwidth & latency breakdown / next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Private deployment: bandwidth & latency breakdown / next steps

Hi Rajiv / FinVest ops team,

Great call earlier — thanks for walking through the workload. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can scope the Private deployment acceptance tests. I focused this on the performance and network items we agreed to validate:

Summary of requirements we heard from you:
- Target P95 tail latency (inference response time): <= 200 ms for short-chat flows (~64 tokens).
- P95 for longer generations (up to 512 tokens): <= 800 ms.
- Sustained throughput: ~5000 tokens/sec aggregate (across typical business hours).
- Concurrency baseline: 40 simultaneous active sessions with streaming chunks (websocket-style).
- Streaming chunk latency goal: inter-chunk <= 50 ms where possible (end-to-end).
- Egress & network: VPN with IPSec is OK for now; you may prefer VPC Peering for lower variance.

What we (Redwood) will provide for the network validation:
- A short network test plan (iperf/traceroute/packet capture checklist) and an ip range list for egress. Attachment: network-test-instructions.pdf
- Egress IPs for our private endpoints (CSV attached). Attachment: redwood-egress-ips.csv
- A test harness that simulates your typical request mix (chat + up-to-512-token generations).

Immediate asks for your team:
1) Please confirm whether you want to run tests over the VPN tunnel or set up VPC peering (peering is preferred if you can open a maintenance window).
2) Share a preferred 1-hour window next week for an initial iperf/traceroute test and a separate 2-hour window for an end-to-end streaming run (we'll coordinate hosts).
3) Provide a sample payload size distribution (percent of requests <=64 tokens, 65-256, 257-512) so we can tune concurrency and batching.

Acceptance criteria we propose for the first pass (can iterate):
- Network path RTT to our endpoint: median < 20 ms, p95 < 60 ms.
- No packet loss > 0.5% during 5-minute sustained runs.
- Egress bandwidth available: minimum 200 Mbps sustained for the test window.
- Application-level: p95 within 25% of our baseline for equivalent tests in AWS N. Virginia.

I'll loop Karthik on the details for the ip ranges and exact test commands. Marissa will own scheduling/ops coordination from the account team side.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-test-instructions.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); redwood-egress-ips.csv (CSV, 1 page)

Jonas — thanks for the recap, really helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule tests: 

1) On the latency targets: is the p95 <=200ms goal assuming cold start or warm KV-cache? For our chat flow most sessions are short-lived and we care about 95th across warm sessions.
2) For streaming chunk latency: are you recommending a specific chunk size (tokens per chunk / ms window)? Our frontend uses websocket streaming and we'd like to match chunk sizing to reduce perceived latency.
3) For peering vs VPN: we prefer VPC peering (we're on AWS) but would need a clear list of required routes and any NACL/security group changes.

We'll get you the payload distribution tomorrow. Tentatively good for initial iperf on Tue 09/14 10:00-11:00 AM PDT; can do the end-to-end streaming run Wed 09/15 01:00-03:00 PM PDT (if that works for Redwood).

Also quick compliance Q: during the network test are you capturing any payloads? We need to ensure PII is never forwarded to Redwood test infra.

— Rajiv
Director, Platform Engineering
FinVest Analytics

Hey Rajiv — tagging onto Jonas' note with the technical checklist and answers.

Short answers:
- Latency baseline: the targets Jonas documented assume warm KV cache (i.e., the model weights are resident and KV cache for the session is primed). Cold-starts (server spin-up or model swap) will add several hundred ms and are out of scope for the streaming SLO.
- Streaming chunk sizing: we typically recommend 32-64 tokens per chunk or a 40-80 ms cadence for UIs that expect near-instant feedback. For your websocket flow, aim for ~50 token chunks as a starting point.
- Peering specifics: for AWS VPC peering we need you to share the consuming VPC CIDR and a maintenance window. We'll provide the exact route entries and the list of egress / load-balancer IPs (CSV attached).

Network test commands (shortlist):
- iperf3: run server on your VM, client from our test host; 60s runs, parallel streams=8, report avg and p95 bandwidth.
- traceroute (mtr): 5-minute mtr run to our egress IP; collect p50/p95 RTT and packet-loss samples.
- tcpdump: 60s capture during a simulated streaming session to check MTU/TCP segmentation/retransmits.

Egress / TLS notes:
- We terminate TLS at our private endpoint inside your peered VPC (mutual TLS option available).
- MTU: default 1500 is fine; if you have jumbo frames let us know and we'll adapt (we recommend avoiding fragmentation).

Expected test metrics and pass thresholds for the initial run: (we'll adapt after first pass)
- Network: median RTT < 20 ms; p95 RTT < 60 ms; packet loss < 0.5% for 5-minute runs.
- Bandwidth: sustained >= 200 Mbps during parallel iperf runs if you expect >5000 tokens/sec. If you expect higher token throughput, scale linearly (e.g., 5000 tokens/sec ~= ~300 Mbps depending on payload size).
- Application: 95th response time for 64-token responses should be within 200 ms; for 512-token responses within 800 ms.

Attachments: redwood-egress-ips.csv (egress IP list), network-test-instructions.pdf (iperf/mtr/tcpdump commands + example results).

Privacy: we will not request or capture any real PII payloads. For end-to-end streaming runs, please use synthetic payloads that mimic sizes and token distributions but contain no customer data.

Next steps:
- I'll upload the egress IPs to the Drive link Jonas included.
- Rajiv: confirm Tue/Wed windows above and share VPC CIDR for peering prep.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
